DEVICE DESCRIPTION
The HAMILTON-Ti is designed for adults and pediatrics requiring invasive or noninvasive
ventilation support. Due to its compact design, a fully-loaded weight of only 6.5 kg (14.3 Ibs),
a twin hot-swappable battery supply, and a built-in turbine; the HAMILTON-Ti can
accompany a ventilated patient everywhere within the hospital or outside the hospital when
transport is needed. The HAMILTON-Ti can run using AC or DC power. It does not need
C compressed air or 02 to drive the pneumatics, which reduces the weight load in the aircraft
needed to operate the ventilator.
FK7Z Since the HAMILTON-Ti has been tested and evaluated for flight and high-altitude
environments, it can be also used during patient transfer by emergency rescue vehicles,
fixed-wing aircraft, or helicopter. This makes the HAMILTON-Ti especially relevant for
Aeromedical Evacuations and Medevac operations.
The HAMILTON-Ti ventilator uses the same graphical user interface (GUI) used by the
HAMILTON-C2 and HAMILTON-G5, featuring a touchscreen "Ventilation Cockpit'; this
C provides the exact information that the user needs and helps focus on what is importanlt. In
addition, the HAMILTON-Ti includes the ASV venti lation- mode which automatically applies
WA lung-protective strategies, reduces the risk of operator error, and promotes early weaning.
The HAMILTON-Ti's microprocessor system controls gas delivery and monitors the patient.
The gas delivery and monitoring functions are cross-checked by an alarm controller. This
cross-checking helps prevent simultaneous failure of these two main functions and
minimizes the possible hazards of software failure.
The HAMILTON-Ti is intended as a transport ventilator, based on the existing HAMILTON-
W C2, with minor adaptations to make the HAMILTON-Ti capable of being used in high-
altitude flight environments. The HAMILTON-Ti's changes include the following:
1 . The HAMILTON-Ti software is identical to the HAMILTON-C2's software, except that
some of the options are not available with the HAMILTON-Ti, (e.g. Neonatal Ventilation
& nCPAP-PS). Other features like Trends & Loops, NIV, NIV-ST, APRV, and DuoPAP
are standard with the 02, but are only optional with the HAMILTON-Ti.
2. The HAMILTON-Ti has increased immunity from EMI, including >30 V/in. It also has
extra safety features for the EMO, ESO, and REI environments fournd on aircraft.
U3. The unit is contained within an impact resistant case which protects the controls from damage and inadvertent manipulation. The enclosure for the HAMILTON-Ti has been NoCmnpAr ruggedized to withstand shock, vibrations, water ingress, and drops from >1 meter
M heights.
4. The HAMILTON-Ti was tested for use in fixed and rotary-wing aircraft.. Because
mechanical ventilation can be challenging during air-medical transport, particularly due
to the impact of changing barometric pressure with different altitude levels, the
HAMILTON-Ti automatically compensates for altitude changes. Adjusting provided- and
U measured-patient volumes accordingly, thereby eliminating the need for manualcalculation and reducing the risk of error.
HOSW9 5. The HAMILTON-Ti has a "lock-button" which prevents an inadvertent change of
settings. If screen lock is active, the following items are inactive: Touchscreen,
Power/Standby switch, Print-screen key, Press-and-turn knob. Active are Alarm Silence,
Manual Breath, 02 enrichment, Nebulizer. To switch off power, the user must press the
On/Off button for > 3 s.

INTENDED USE
The HAMILTON-Ti ventilator is intended to provide positive pressure ventilatory support to
adults and pediatrics.
Intended areas of use:
* In the intensive care ward or in the recovery room.
o For emergency medical care or primary care.
* During transport within and outside the hospital.
* During transfer by rescue vehicles, jet orhelicopter.
The HAMILTON-Ti ventilator is a medical device intended for use by qualified, trained
personnel under the direction of a p hysician and within the limits of its stated technical
Cspecifications.
FAA REGULATIONS
In accordance with the US Department of Transportation (DOT) and the Federal Aviation
Administration (FAA), along with their rules on the 'Use of Respiratory Assistive Devices on
Aircraft", the HAMILTON-Ti meets the applicable safety requirements for Medical Portable
a + Electronic Devices (M-PED) by not exceeding the maximum level of radiated radio
frequency interference as described in the RTCAJDO 160F. Section 21, Category M.
DISCUSSION ON THE NON-CLINICAL TESTS
The non-clinical test results show that the HAMILTON-Ti is safe and effective for its
intended use. The ventilator was further subjected to waveform performance testing as
described in the standard ASTM Fl 100-90. The results of the software verification and
validation testing demonstrate that all specified requirements have been implemented
correctly and completely.

The intended use statement for the HAM ILTON-Ti ventilator is equivalent to the p red icate
device. The technological characteristics (i.e., design, material, energy source) and
performance specifications of the HAMILTON-Ti ventilator are equivalent to those of the
predicate device. One of the tests used to evaluate the HAMILTON-Ti in a high-altitude,
low-pressure environment, was to place the HAMILTON-Ti inside an altitude chamber to
test the effects on the sensors and the ventilator measurements & read Ings.
The intended use of the HAMILTON-Ti is covered by the referenced, predicate device. The
technical characteristics of the HAMILTON-Ti do not raise any new questions regarding the
safety or effectiveness of ventilators. The HAMILTON-Ti's software has gone through
verification/validation tests. A complete revision level history, hazard analysis, and a
traceability analysis linking requirements to validation were done. The conclusions drawn
from the non-clinical tests demonstrate that the HAMILTON-Ti is as safe, as effective, and
performs as well as the legally marketed device. The HAMILTON-Ti is, therefore,
considered to be substantially equivalent to the currently marketed predicate device which
has been previously cleared by FDA.
